newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Bezeq lowered to sell.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Bezeq lowered to sell.

text.p: Bank Hapoalim has lowered Bezeq Israel Telecom's rating from hold to sell, the bank said in a report on Tuesday.

Hapoalim analyst Dany Koninsky said that Bezeq was expected to have slower growth in revenues and a further erosion of profitability because of the structural changes in the telecom sector in Israel and the end of the company's monopoly in certain areas.
Hapoalim valued the company between $1.76 to $1.99 billion.

"A number of fields in which Bezeq is active have been opened to competition, among which the cellular phone sector... whereby the tender for the third operator will be published by July 1997 and the international lines sector, whereby competitors will start operating in July 1997," the report said.
The local lines sector is also due to be opened to competition by 1999, the report said.

Hapoalim estimated Bezeq revenues would reach 8.6 billion shekels in 1997, up from 8.5 billion in 1996. Net profit in 1997 is estimated at 538 million shekels, down from 676 million in 1996. Earnings per share (EPS) in 1997 are an estimated 0.73 shekels against 0.92 shekels in 1996.
Revenues for 1998 are estimated at 8.77 billion shekels and EPS at 0.70 shekels, the report said.
